decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with enhanced mechanical properties, such as strength, ductility, and corrosion resistance. Recent studies have explored the effects of processing techniques, such as spark plasma sintering, mechanical alloying, and stationary friction processing, on the microstructure and properties of HEAs. Additionally, the role of chemical short-range order (SRO) in influencing the mobility mechanisms of dislocations in HEAs has been investigated.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in developing HEAs, there is still a need to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off and achieve a balance between these properties. Furthermore, the oxidation behavior of HEAs at high temperatures remains a concern, and the development of HEAs with enhanced catalytic activity and durability for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) is an open question.
decision.why: Grain refinement has been shown to improve the mechanical properties and corrosion resistance of HEAs. By tailoring the microstructure through processing techniques, such as stationary friction processing, it may be possible to achieve a balance between strength and ductility. Additionally, grain refinement can enhance the catalytic activity and durability of HEAs for HER and HOR by increasing the surface area and reducing the defect density.
